subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw expose a global `openclaw agent --dry-run`, and what exact execution surfaces must it cover before users can treat it as a safety boundary?
rationale: Current source shows Gateway-first CLI dispatch, embedded tools, client-hosted tools, CLI backends, and Codex dynamic/native tool paths; automation can prove the gap but cannot choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Define bounded v1 contract
options.body: Approve covered surfaces, preview result shape, hook ordering, and explicit unsupported-surface behavior before implementation.

options.title: Fold into safe workflow modes
options.body: Use the broader Ask/Plan/Modify work as the product umbrella while preserving this issue as the focused tool-preview requirement.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep scoped dry-runs and policy hooks as the supported execution-safety path, then close this direction after maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Define bounded v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve covered surfaces, preview result shape, hook ordering, and explicit unsupported-surface behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The broadest live history signal spans agent tool adapter, agent-core execution, and Codex dynamic tool safety surfaces.
